passage: On Monday night, Sahil's socks lay in a heap on the floor. On Tuesday morning he found one blue sock and looked under the bed, in the drawer and inside his shoe. "It's gone." He climbed into bed and pulled the blanket over his head. "I'm not going." Kavitha, his mother, coaxed and called but the time ran out. On Thursday, the second sock turned up inside a trouser leg in the wash. By then Sahil had missed assembly and had stood at the back of the class.

qa.q: What did Sahil say after climbing back into bed?
What was Sahil feeling when he could not find the second sock?
qa.a: Sahil felt frustrated and helpless. He looked in several places and then pulled the blanket over his head.

qa.q: What could Sahil try when an item is missing, and why?
qa.a: He could ask for help finding it, or wear another pair. One missing sock is a small problem and should not stop the whole morning.

qa.q: How does the morning look to Kavitha?
qa.a: Kavitha sees a child who quit and a rush that could have been avoided. Being late costs the whole class time as well as assembly.

grounding: A child cannot find the second sock, climbs back into bed and refuses to go, so one missing item ends the morning's plan.
